gloss: special news bulletin; breaking news; emergency broadcast

definitions.gloss: special news bulletin; breaking news; emergency broadcast
definitions.explanation: Used when regular programming is interrupted for urgent news.

examples.japanese: {臨時|りんじ}ニュースをお{伝|つた}えします。
examples.english: We bring you a special news bulletin.

examples.japanese: {番組|ばんぐみ}の{途中|とちゅう}ですが、{臨時|りんじ}ニュースです。
examples.english: We interrupt this program for a special news bulletin.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{直後|ちょくご}、テレビで{臨時|りんじ}ニュースが{流|なが}れた。
examples.english: Right after the earthquake, a special news bulletin aired on TV.

notes:
A compound of {臨時|りんじ} (extraordinary/special) and ニュース (news). Used for urgent broadcasts that interrupt regular programming, typically for natural disasters, major incidents, or critical announcements.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {臨時|りんじ}ニュースをお{伝|つた}えします: standard announcer phrase for breaking news
- {臨時|りんじ}ニュースが{入|はい}る: a news bulletin comes in
- {臨時|りんじ}ニュースが{流|なが}れる: a news bulletin airs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {速報|そくほう}: breaking news flash (shorter, more urgent)
- {特報|とくほう}: special report (emphasis on exclusivity)
- {緊急速報|きんきゅうそくほう}: emergency alert (used for earthquake warnings, etc.)

USAGE:
The phrase {臨時|りんじ}ニュースをお{伝|つた}えします is one of the most recognizable formulaic expressions in Japanese broadcasting. Hearing it on TV or radio immediately signals a serious event.
